messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Strange bias in toy model
parts:
Hi all --

I might be trying to do something impossible, but I would like to use 
random data generated in the transformed data block--draws used 
for monte carlo integration within my model. I'm currently using draws 
from R and passing them in as data, so thought I might be able to 
save time by doing it in the model. 

Unsure whether I could use _rng in the transformed parameter block, 
I coded up the following toy example: 

data {
  int T;
}
transformed data {
  vector[T] out;
  
  for(t in 1:T) {
    out[t] = normal_rng(0 , 1);
  }
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower = 0> sig;
}
model {
  out ~ normal(mu, sig);
}

It compiles and runs fine. But it gives me some really strangely 
biased estimates for mu. When the sample size T is low, the 
estimates of mu are centered on .3. I ran the attached file a couple
of times and got back precisely the same chart. 

It makes me think that the seed for random number generation in 
the transformed data block is fixed. Might this be the case? 

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Strange bias in toy model

Yes, it's allowed, but we have an outstanding issue with it that
it uses different RNGs in each chain, so you can't expect
convergence according to Rhat until we fix that:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2014

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Strange bias in toy model
parts:
Hmm. Looks like that bug may have been fixed, leading to
the unexpected behavior you're seeing.

You have to be careful about what you mean by biased. If
I generate 100 draws from normal(0, 1), it might have a mean
of 0.2. The estimator that then estimes a mean of 0.2 isn't
biased.

It looks like the bug is exactly the opposite of what we
listed now --- it doesn't even take the seed into account.
I'll amend the issue.

But it does look like everything's working as intended as far as RNGs
and samplers are concerned. I amended your program to calculate
the sample mean and sd of the pseudo-random numbers and get this:

data {
int<lower=0> N;
}
transformed data {
vector[N] y;
for (n in 1:N)
y[n] = normal_rng(0, 1);
}
parameters {
real mu;
real<lower = 0> sigma;
}
model {
y ~ normal(mu, sigma);
}
generated quantities {
real mean_y = mean(y);
real sd_y = sd(y);
}

When I set N=100, I indeed see that the RNG is generating a sample
on the high side of average:

N=100:

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
mu 0.20 0.00 0.10 -0.01 0.13 0.20 0.27 0.41 4000 1
sigma 1.03 0.00 0.08 0.90 0.98 1.03 1.08 1.19 3676 1
mean_y 0.20 0.00 0.00 0.20 0.20 0.20 0.20 0.20 2 1
sd_y 1.02 0.00 0.00 1.02 1.02 1.02 1.02 1.02 2 1
lp__ -52.42 0.02 1.01 -55.20 -52.82 -52.09 -51.69 -51.44 1796 1


N=1000:

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
mu 0.01 0.00 0.03 -0.05 -0.01 0.01 0.03 0.07 3411 1
sigma 0.99 0.00 0.02 0.94 0.97 0.98 1.00 1.03 3672 1
mean_y 0.01 0.00 0.00 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 2 1
sd_y 0.98 0.00 0.00 0.98 0.98 0.98 0.98 0.98 2 1
lp__ -485.32 0.03 1.02 -488.09 -485.70 -484.98 -484.61 -484.35 1485 1

- Bob
